title: Foster-care grants missed oversight and used a nine-year-old overhead proposal

beats.text: One San Francisco foster-care grant line carried two audit findings.

visual.sub: One large foster-care spending line carried two findings

beats.text: It reported $28,963,306 in spending for fiscal 2011.
That figure measures the program, not an identified improper payment.

visual.kicker: One large foster-care spending line carried two findings

beats.text: In 2012 the auditor explained both findings in a televised hearing.

visual.kicker: Required oversight of some organizations never occurred

beats.text: Some organizations were left out of monitoring because requirements were misinterpreted.

visual.kicker: Required oversight of some organizations never occurred

beats.text: The auditor attributed the qualified compliance opinion to that oversight failure.

visual.kicker: Required oversight of some organizations never occurred

beats.text: A separate finding involved the overhead rate in the reimbursement claim.

visual.kicker: The reimbursement claim used a cost proposal from nine years earlier

beats.text: The City based its fiscal 2011 claim on a fiscal 2002 proposal.
The auditor did not give the dollar effect or direction of the error.

visual.kicker: The reimbursement claim used a cost proposal from nine years earlier

beats.text: The following year the federal filing recorded an unqualified foster-care opinion.

visual.kicker: The next fiscal-year filing shows an unqualified foster-care opinion

beats.text: That filing does not establish repayment or a correction to the earlier claim.
